comparator.name: Pharmaceutical Sciences (Farmaceutische Wetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch full-time 2026–2027 bachelor has no formal graduation specialisations: 60 EC in each of Years 1–2, then two compulsory 6 EC courses, an 18 EC project and 30 EC open study. The adopted OER Article11.3 controls year allocation; the recruitment page mixes differently named chemistry units and places the modern-developments project differently. No duplicate old/new course versions are stacked. Zero-credit laboratory safety, Dutch diagnostic/remedial language study and mentorship/tutorials are recorded separately. BSA normally requires42first-yearEC. The basic pharmacochemistry practical precedes bioanalysis, molecular pharmacology, toxicology, molecular modelling and synthesis practicals. Project entry requires all first-year courses, all listed practicals including modelling, and120EC including open study for periods5–6. The exceptional periods2–3 project requires every other curricular course passed by31August. Project allocation considers preferences, motivation and capacity; apply by the published early-January deadline and register for XB_0140, Canvas and Onstage. Individual laboratory journal, thesis, talk and poster are required. Academic/professional attitude, practical execution, report and oral presentation each contribute25%; each must reach5.5. Open choices require prior board approval except stated university/listed-minor exemptions, at least12ECat300 and at most6ECat100; an overseas package can include one6ECmaster course that cannot be reused for a subsequent master. Attendance conditions follow individual manuals; honours and historic transition units are not additional requirements.

exception.reason: The strongest attempted UCR programme has real contributions in pharmacology, molecular-cell biology, biochemistry and biomedical laboratory methods. Pharmacology explicitly teaches targets, drug–macromolecule interactions and quantitative pharmacokinetic models; these contributions are retained in the evidence. However, the completed composition is organised predominantly around disease biology, general neuroscience and general data/research methods. It does not implement the target’s defining progression from chemical structure/reactivity through synthesis, compound identification, bioanalysis/toxicology practicals and pharmaceutical molecular/computational modelling to experimental drug discovery. Generic machine learning, neural networks, anatomy, immunity and evidence synthesis cannot supply those missing chemical mechanisms and experimental design skills. Adding available recycling/inorganic chemistry or ecology does not establish medicinal/organic chemistry. A coherent biomedical programme is therefore not by itself a substantive pharmaceutical-sciences response. No defensible complete UCR alternative is established; this is not based on a matching-course quota, professional licensing or absence of a degree title.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: All24selected actual enriched profiles read. HCBBIOM3117.5EC directly teaches pharmacokinetics/targets; HCBLIFE211/213/21422.5EC add cell/biochemical/basiclaboratory contributions. The remaining24course180EC construction adds disease/brain biology, statistics, generic computing, ethics and PPD, without a sustained chemical discovery sequence. A full-workbook search found no organic/medicinal chemistry or synthesis progression; ENSDELT311 inorganic recycling and ENSECOL212 ecological use of chemistry are not substitutes. The original proposal and every selected profile are retained in QC evidence.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Pharmaceutical Sciences studies the early stages of drug discovery through molecular biology and chemistry. Students learn to identify drug targets, design and synthesise compounds, test their activity and safety, and conduct pharmaceutical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers relevant study in pharmacology, biochemistry, molecular-cell biology and biomedical laboratory methods. Its Pharmacology course includes drug targets and quantitative pharmacokinetics. These contributions do not form a complete programme centred on medicinal chemistry, synthesis, compound testing and pharmaceutical molecular modelling. We therefore show the verified VU curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.
